questions.question: The standard test for the lower fibres of trapezius is performed with the patient:

options.A: Supine with the arm at the side
options.D: Prone, arm overhead in line with the lower trapezius fibres, lifting the arm against resistance

questions.explanation: Lower trapezius depresses and upwardly rotates the scapula; the arm position (about 145° abduction) aligns the fibres.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Weakness of the rhomboids is demonstrated by:

options.B: Weak scapular adduction and downward rotation, with the scapula lying lateral to the spine

questions.explanation: Tested prone with the hand on the buttock lifting the scapula; dorsal scapular nerve (C5).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The latissimus dorsi is tested in prone with the arm:

options.D: Medially rotated and adducted, extending the shoulder against resistance

questions.explanation: Thoracodorsal nerve (C6–C8).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the curl-up (upper abdominal) manual muscle test, the arm position that makes the test hardest and is used for a normal (grade 5) result is:
questions.explanation: The further the arms are from the hips, the greater the load on the abdominals: hands behind the head = normal (5), arms crossed on the chest = good (4), arms extended forward = fair (3) (Kendall).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Hip flexion against gravity (grade 3) is tested with the patient:

options.C: Sitting, lifting the thigh off the plinth with the knee flexed

questions.explanation: The iliopsoas is the prime mover; sartorius and rectus femoris assist.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In testing tibialis anterior, the examiner resists:

options.C: Dorsiflexion with inversion of the foot

questions.explanation: Extensor digitorum longus lifts the toes; with eversion peroneus tertius also works.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The peroneus longus and brevis are tested by resisting:

options.B: Eversion with plantar flexion in side-lying

questions.explanation: Superficial peroneal nerve (L5–S1).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Testing the soleus in isolation requires the knee to be:

options.A: Flexed to about 90° to slacken the gastrocnemius

questions.explanation: Gastrocnemius is tested with the knee extended.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Biceps brachii is best isolated as an elbow flexor when the forearm is:
questions.explanation: Brachioradialis acts best in neutral and brachialis in pronation.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A patient who cannot extend the elbow against gravity but can do so gravity-eliminated has triceps grade:
questions.explanation: Gravity-eliminated full range = grade 2.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Opposition of the thumb is performed mainly by the:
questions.explanation: Adductor pollicis is ulnar nerve supplied.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Wrist extension with radial deviation is produced mainly by the:

options.C: Extensor carpi radialis longus and brevis

questions.explanation: Radial nerve; ECU gives extension with ulnar deviation.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Testing the serratus anterior in supine involves:

options.A: Pushing the arm toward the ceiling (protraction) against resistance

questions.explanation: Weakness shows as winging when pushing against a wall.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the standard test for neck flexors the patient lies:

options.C: Supine, flexing the neck (chin tuck) against resistance applied at the forehead

questions.explanation: Sternocleidomastoid and deep neck flexors; stabilise the chest.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The normal range of elbow flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Soft tissue approximation limits flexion; extension 0° (hard end feel).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Normal forearm pronation and supination each measure about:
questions.explanation: Starting position: elbow flexed to 90° with the forearm in neutral, thumb up.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The normal range of wrist flexion (palmar flexion) is about:
questions.explanation: Wrist extension 0–70°; radial deviation 0–20°; ulnar deviation 0–30°.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The normal range of knee flexion is about:
questions.explanation: Passive flexion limited by soft tissue approximation of the calf and thigh.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Hip rotation range is best measured with the patient:

options.C: Sitting or supine with hip and knee flexed to 90°

questions.explanation: Axis at the centre of the patella, fixed arm perpendicular to the floor.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Normal cervical rotation to each side is approximately:
questions.explanation: Cervical flexion 45–60°, extension 70°, lateral flexion 45°.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The modified Schober test measures:

options.B: Lumbar spine flexion (increase in the skin distance between marks above and below the lumbosacral junction)

questions.explanation: A normal increase is more than 5 cm over a 10-cm line; reduced in ankylosing spondylitis.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The finger-to-floor distance test assesses:

options.A: Combined spinal and hip flexion mobility

questions.explanation: Limited by tight hamstrings as well as lumbar stiffness.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Chest expansion in ankylosing spondylitis is typically reduced to less than:
questions.explanation: Measured at the fourth intercostal space between full inspiration and expiration.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the elbow is:
questions.explanation: Pronation and supination are equally preserved in a pure elbow capsular pattern.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the talocrural (ankle) joint is:

options.A: Plantar flexion limited more than dorsiflexion
options.D: Dorsiflexion limited more than plantar flexion

questions.explanation: Subtalar joint: increasing varus (limited inversion eversion pattern).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the wrist joint is:

options.D: Equal limitation of flexion and extension

questions.explanation: Cyriax: wrist equal limitation of flexion and extension, with the radial deviation more limited than ulnar.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The capsular pattern of the cervical spine is:

options.B: Loss of flexion and rotation only
options.C: Equal limitation of side flexion and rotation with some loss of extension

questions.explanation: Seen in osteoarthritis.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A non-capsular pattern of limitation is usually caused by:

options.B: Internal derangement, ligamentous adhesion or extra-articular lesion

questions.explanation: Examples: loose body, ligament sprain.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The close-packed position of the knee is full extension; the resting (loose-packed) position is about:
questions.explanation: Resting position is used for assessing joint play and for mobilisation to relieve pain.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The resting (loose-packed) position of the hip joint is:

options.D: 30° flexion, 30° abduction and slight lateral rotation

questions.explanation: Close-packed is extension, internal rotation and abduction.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The close-packed position of the wrist (radiocarpal) joint is:
questions.explanation: Resting position is neutral with slight ulnar deviation.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The close-packed position of the ankle joint is:
questions.explanation: Resting position: about 10° plantar flexion, midway between inversion and eversion.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Maitland Grade II mobilisation is:

options.A: A small oscillation at the end of range
options.C: A large-amplitude oscillation within the range, not reaching resistance
options.D: A small-amplitude oscillation at the start of the range

questions.explanation: Grade I: small amplitude at the beginning of range; Grade II: large amplitude within the free range.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Maitland Grade III mobilisation is:

options.B: A large-amplitude oscillation up to the limit of range into resistance
options.C: A small-amplitude oscillation within the free range

questions.explanation: Used to stretch stiff tissues.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: In the Kaltenborn system, a Grade III traction or glide is applied to:

options.A: Stretch the joint capsule and surrounding tissue

questions.explanation: Grade I (loosening), II (tighten/slack), III (stretch).
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Mulligan's mobilisation with movement (MWM) is performed:

options.B: With a sustained accessory glide while the patient actively moves the painful joint, pain-free
options.D: With the patient relaxed and passive

questions.explanation: Techniques include NAGs, SNAGs and MWMs.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Cyriax's manipulation techniques are based on the principle that:

options.D: Lumbar disc displacements can be reduced by traction and manipulation with a graded approach

questions.explanation: Selective tension to localise the lesion; then treat with techniques such as transverse frictions.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The physiological effect of axial joint traction applied to a painful joint is:

options.C: Reduction of compression and pain relief via mechanoreceptor stimulation

questions.explanation: Grade I–II traction reduces pain; Grade III stretches.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: To improve inspiration range of a rib, the examiner mobilises the rib:
questions.explanation: Costovertebral joint mobilisation is part of thoracic treatment.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: For thoracic kyphosis stiffness, extension of the thoracic spine can be encouraged by:

options.D: Posteroanterior (central) pressures with the patient in prone

questions.explanation: PA glides are the classic Maitland technique.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Mobilisation is contraindicated in:

options.A: Acute inflammation, malignancy, infection and unstable fracture

questions.explanation: Also severe osteoporosis and hypermobility.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Myofascial release aims to:

options.D: Release restrictions in the fascia through sustained low-load pressure and stretch

questions.explanation: Held for 90–120 seconds until release is felt.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The empty can (Jobe) test assesses the:
questions.explanation: Arm abducted to 90° in the scapular plane, thumbs down, resisted elevation.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Gerber lift-off test evaluates the:
questions.explanation: The hand is placed on the back and lifted away from the lumbar spine.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Speed's test is positive when pain over the bicipital groove is reproduced by:

options.B: Resisted shoulder flexion with the elbow extended and forearm supinated

questions.explanation: Indicates biceps tendinitis.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive hornblower's sign indicates a tear of the:
questions.explanation: The patient cannot externally rotate the arm at 90° abduction.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive sulcus sign (depression below the acromion on downward traction) indicates:
questions.explanation: Associated with multidirectional instability.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A patient with recurrent anterior shoulder dislocation will resist the examiner's movement of the arm into:
questions.explanation: This is the apprehension test.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A valgus stress test of the elbow assesses the:
questions.explanation: Throwers are prone to UCL injury.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Bunnell–Littler test checks for:

options.D: Tightness of the intrinsic muscles of the hand

questions.explanation: Inability to flex the PIP joint when the MCP is held extended indicates intrinsic tightness.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Allen's test evaluates:

options.D: Patency of the radial and ulnar arteries

questions.explanation: The patient clenches the fist while both arteries are occluded; release one and observe colour return.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Watson (scaphoid shift) test assesses:
questions.explanation: Pressure over the scaphoid tubercle during radial deviation produces a painful clunk.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Apley's grinding and distraction test in the prone position is used to differentiate:

options.D: Meniscal injury (compression pain) from ligament injury (distraction pain)

questions.explanation: Compression with rotation reproduces pain in meniscal tears.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Clarke's sign (patellar grind test) is positive in:
questions.explanation: Pain on quadriceps contraction against patellar compression.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The posterior sag sign (Godfrey's test) indicates injury of the:
questions.explanation: With hips and knees flexed to 90°, the tibia sags backward.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The pivot shift test assesses:

options.A: Anterolateral rotatory instability due to ACL deficiency

questions.explanation: A subluxation then reduction is felt as the knee flexes from extension.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The windlass test is positive in:
questions.explanation: Passive extension of the great toe reproduces heel pain by tensioning the plantar fascia.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: The Silfverskiold test differentiates tightness of the:
questions.explanation: Dorsiflexion is compared with the knee flexed and extended.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Kemp's (quadrant) test provokes pain in:

options.D: Lumbar facet joint pathology and nerve root compression

questions.explanation: Extension with rotation and side-flexion.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: A positive Valsalva manoeuvre for spinal pathology reproduces:

options.B: Radicular pain due to increased intrathecal pressure (e.g. space-occupying lesion or disc)

questions.explanation: Bearing down raises intrathecal pressure.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Hoffmann's sign (flexion of the thumb and index finger on flicking the middle fingernail) indicates:

options.B: Upper motor neurone lesion (e.g. cervical myelopathy)

questions.explanation: Pathological reflex in cord compression.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Relief of arm pain on manual cervical distraction suggests:
questions.explanation: Foraminal opening decompresses the root.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: Normal two-point discrimination at the fingertip is about:
questions.explanation: Back: 40–70 mm; palm 8–12 mm.
questions.sourceBook: Magee, Orthopedic Physical Assessment; Daniels & Worthingham's Muscle Testing; Kaltenborn, Manual Mobilization of the Joints; Maitland's Peripheral Manipulation (chapter-level reference; cross-checked with Suraj Kumar, MCQs for MPT Entrance Examination, 2e)

questions.question: On a 0–4 grading scale, a deep tendon reflex graded 2+ is:
questions.explanation: 0 absent, 1+ diminished, 2+ normal, 3+ brisk, 4+ clonus.

questions.question: The olfactory nerve is cranial nerve number:
